[Music] My name is Tiji Justo. Once again, I am truly grateful to Kreupasanam for lifting us up as permanent witnesses of Mother Mary's apparition.
This is my husband, Justo Paulose. This is his younger brother, his brother’s wife, and their child. I first entered the Covenant in January 2022.
From that day until now, it’s been three and a half years that I have been living in the Covenant without a break.
Right now, we have come from Canada just to share this testimony.
We are here only for the purpose of giving testimony.
I had given my testimony once before, and after that I went to Canada. Even after going there, I continued to take the Covenant online consistently for three months.
Now that I’ve come here again, I renewed the Covenant. My very first testimony, you could say, was for my husband’s younger brother’s family.
Both of them — husband and wife — are deaf and mute. They took the Covenant along with us, but due to their physical limitations, they were not able to renew it later.
It’s been seven years since they got married, and even after all this time...
...they have not yet been able to renew the Covenant.
They didn’t have children — that was their main intention. Later, due to their limitations, they were not able to renew the Covenant or engage in its practices.
So I decided to place that calling into my own Covenant.
I carried the burden in my own heart and prayed on their behalf through the Covenant seal placed on my womb.
Even after I went to Canada, I continued to do this prayer consistently.
I spiritually imagined my womb as my sister-in-law’s and kept praying with the Covenant seal for her. They too were praying.
They tried many treatments — allopathy, homeopathy — there was no form of treatment they didn’t attempt.
But in the end, when nothing worked, they began to fall into a deep depression.
They reached a point where they didn’t want to see anyone or face anyone — completely withdrawn.
That’s when I prayed very strongly in the Covenant, because God had already allowed many limitations in their lives. If He also denied them this one blessing…
…I feared what their condition might become. That’s why I prayed, “Even if my own intention is fulfilled, Lord, please fulfill this one for them too.”
I specifically prayed that there should be a sign from Mother Mary and a sign from the Covenant in this.
As part of that, in October 2023, we had the Rosary Month devotion at our homes — we bring Mother Mary’s statue, pray, and chant the rosary together.
During that time, my husband’s mother told my sister-in-law to receive the statue of Mother Mary.
When my sister-in-law took the statue of Mother Mary, she felt a kind of shock, like a jolt, in her hand.
She experienced it like an electric vibration in her arm.
When she told this to her mother, her mother said, “That must be Mother Mary blessing you.”
The very next day, they did a test — this was in October — and she was confirmed pregnant.
And just as it happened, in May 2024, God blessed them with a healthy baby boy.
Even though both parents have disabilities, the child is completely healthy.
As the father often says, this is truly a miracle of the Covenant and of Mother Mary.
October and May are the most important months related to the Covenant in our life. It was in October we came to know she was pregnant, and in May, we received the sign of the Covenant in the form of our child.
That is the greatest testimony. Now the second testimony is about us receiving PR in Canada.
We had gone to Canada on a study visa.
Anyone living in Canada knows how incredibly hard it is to get PR now.
Many are returning to their home countries because of the difficulties.
Even for those who eventually get PR, it usually takes four to five years.
But in our case, by God’s great grace, my husband got a job soon after we arrived. We reached Canada during a heavy winter.
The very next month, he got a job at a tire repair division of a U.S. automobile company that supports PR.
By God’s grace, he didn’t have to work survival jobs or restaurant jobs.
He is from the mechanical field, and this tire repair job was within his area of expertise and supported PR.
But there were many challenges involved. The first hurdle was passing IELTS.
Since my husband was from the automobile field here in India, he had never even dreamed of having to pass something like IELTS.
He didn’t know the language. He had never thought of writing or passing such a test.
He never studied IT or anything like that — passing IELTS wasn’t something he imagined. But I had placed it in the Covenant.
I encouraged him boldly to write it, and with the strength of the Covenant alone, he was blessed to receive the required score.
The next step was getting WES done, because he had studied here in India.
His diploma in the automobile field from here needed an equivalency certificate in Canada.
Only after receiving that could we move forward. But when we applied for WES,
they responded via email saying it could not be considered equivalent.
And for us to get PR, we were living in a Canadian community called North Bay.
We needed a recommendation letter. We went to the community that provides this recommendation and asked for it. This is how it happened.
They told us that even with this, you won’t get it — it’s a rejection, and they won’t give it to you.
But these were the people who said this to us. Because I have faith as someone who lives and keeps the Covenant,
I told my husband, “It’s not this community, it is Lord Jesus who is the Lord. I have strong faith that my God will give this to me.”
I believe that it is my God, the Holy Mother, who will give it. We decided to move forward with this faith.
So, we applied anyway, even though the file initially came back as rejected. We put on the Covenant oils — the seal oil, kashu oil, salt —
and prayed with strong faith. We applied despite knowing the odds were against us, because those people had said they wouldn’t give it to us.
But by God’s great grace, we received the recommendation.
The next step was applying to IRCC for PR.
The first thing needed was ID proof. My husband submitted the documents, certificates, and so on.
The first requirement was ID proof — that is, a birth certificate.
Since my husband was born at home, we did not have a birth certificate. Many suggested we consult a lawyer to try to do something.
I told them, “We don’t have a lawyer. Our lawyer is the Holy Mother who brought us this far.”
Once we get a lawyer involved, maybe they’ll tell us to do something wrong, or fake something, fabricate documents —
I wasn’t interested in that. We keep praying and believe. My father always says, “Don’t cheat or deceive.”
So I said, “God will provide. We won’t do anything wrong.”
We wrote an explanation letter to the officials explaining the situation, and with the Covenant oil and the sign of the cross,
and praying with faith, and with all the rosary beads used, we applied again.
They had no problems and accepted it.
The next issue, as I mentioned earlier, wes became a problem.
They said it was a problem here and that it was required. We explained our situation.
They told us then provide 10th certificate, but normally here they expect degree certificates and such.
Doing all these things is very rare. We are in Canada, and after a lot of searching, my husband found an agency.
Back home, we had been following up with an agency for about five months, but no matter what we did,
it was impossible to proceed. My husband’s SSLC certificate was delayed for five months,
and neither we nor the agency could get it processed. There were many obstacles. Every month,
we would receive emails from IRCC asking where the certificate was. We’d say it hadn’t arrived yet,
and the next month they’d give us a deadline. This happened five times.
It’s not that they didn’t communicate — they emailed us five times asking for the certificate.
We kept telling them it wasn’t received yet and that the process was ongoing.
Finally, on November 25 last year, we received an email from IRCC giving us one last chance.
They said if the certificate wasn’t submitted by December 25 — exactly a month later — they would close our file permanently and not consider it anymore.
That meant rejection. For us, there were many demerits — our age, gaps in education, and other issues.
So this was the only path we had. Getting PR through a student visa is very, very rare.
This route was completely closed to us when they shut down the program. We had no other options.
The particular program that gave PR was closed, and
we had no choice but to...
We reached a point where there was nothing we could do, and we had to face returning home.
Even then, I did not lose heart because I had strong faith in the Covenant I lived by and a clear understanding.
I told my husband, “Don’t give up at all. This merit is going away, but it’s meant to become a testimony.”
I encouraged him to move forward boldly. Then back home, my father made connections and said we needed to get the documents directly to the exam office.
We had to send it via express courier to get it there on time because Canada Post was on strike.
So, even that route was blocked; the courier didn’t deliver the package.
They said they wouldn’t handle it or process it anymore. Express courier isn’t a normal service here.
But I told my father, “You must go there, pray with salt, only then will it be received.”
Even though he is a praying man, he wasn’t fully convinced about praying with salt.
He said he has some political influence, and that we might get some help, but after going there, we received no assistance at all.
Because it was something that...
It was beyond the authorities’ power — something they were not allowed to do. But he went there,
prayed with salt, and in the end, we received help — God’s help, not political help.
Someone from there went with my father, sent the package by express courier.
I had told him to pray with salt and faith while sending it.
So he did, and his faith grew stronger. The power of praying with salt helped us.
I also prayed like that, and it’s just like that — if I receive it, it’s enough for me.
My greatest desire is for my Lord to take care of everything. It’s not about my own matters.
I prayed this way — if I get it after praying with salt, it’s enough. If it’s rejection, so be it.
That’s exactly how my father did it, and that’s how we received it.
But by the time all this was done, the deadline they gave us was December 25.
When everything was done, it was already December 10.
For five days, we did not receive any mail. We sent it from the Wes; when we called to ask,
they said they received it on December 15, but they were on vacation — the vacation period around New Year.
They said after the vacation, the process would start again, around June 6, 2025.
That would take one or two months. So by the time we got it, it wouldn’t matter; our file would be closed in December.
My husband became discouraged again. We had no way out, no options left.
They said we had no options, and that’s exactly how it was — nothing more we could do.
But even then, I had strong faith. I said this merit is being lost, but it’s meant to be a testimony.
Everything depends on grace, so there’s no reason to fear. I encouraged us to be brave.
When we opened the website, there was a chat box. We didn’t know what it was,
but I wrote a few sentences describing our situation and sent it like a message.
I don’t know what it was exactly, but for me, whatever I submit is done with grace.
Whatever papers I submit, I say, “Holy Mother, this is done with your grace. You have to take this to heaven and request God”
I only send things after getting approval; that’s exactly how I did it. Miraculously,
the next day when we went to church as usual, we received an email from Visa.
It said they would close the file after next month. Within 24 hours,
they confirmed everything was completed and sent a mail. For my husband,
that was like a new life, a turning point. Right then, we prayed to IRCC and uploaded the documents.
They had said on December 25 they would give rejection, but the very IRCC
sent us the pre-arrival invitation for PR on December 24. I don’t have time to explain all the details, but
there were many obstacles and issues. However, on February 18,
they ignored all the criteria and deadlines and said we could not even submit documents.
Even people with merit have difficulties getting PR. Those in Canada know this well.
In this hopeless situation, it was only by Mother’s intervention that the Lord granted us the PR card on February 28.
Once we got it, we could book our flight. This means
we can come here and testify. I have told you,
we came here after many sacrifices. This is the direct way to testify in Canada.
One more thing — even though we are in Canada, we hold a Rosary rally every year. For the past two years,
like here, we do a 12-kilometer rally there. In October, my husband and I
were the only two who conducted the rally. There was a family called Sheena Mithur living with us.
Their work permit and spouse’s application were rejected — Sheena’s application was rejected.
They were told they must leave Canada within three months by mail. This was because their PR was refused.
This happened twice. They had to leave Canada if they didn’t get PR by the date given.
That’s the law there. Otherwise,
they would face serious legal complications and would not be allowed to work.
They didn’t know about Kreupasanam there. They were unaware. They were in Delhi. I introduced them to Kreupasanam.
At that time, in the Rosary rally, even though our own group was small,
our main mission was this. It was with this that we completed the Rosary rally.
Along with many other missions, I told them we have submitted the Rosary  rally. They will get it as soon as possible.
Just as I said, within a week, on Wednesday — Mother’s day — they received an email that they got PR.
This gave them great faith and strength. Then, to testify,
a problem arose between my husband and a friend who was involved financially. It caused us trouble.
It was a loss to us. But that happened only two months ago.
Since then, I have been praying and offering that family. I prayed that it be reconciled. My husband
had no quarrel with the person, nor did that person talk to us.
So I prayed that even if there was a fault on our side and it caused us distress, my husband should go and apologize.
I prayed that the Holy Spirit would work in him and in that person.
We had a flight on Friday. That day my husband had duty and was on a night shift on Thursday.
Even though we had troubles, he went and apologized to that person, and the matter was reconciled.
That person was also very troubled, possibly because of misunderstandings or unknown reasons.
We don’t know exactly. We did not discuss it further, but the problem was resolved in a very peaceful way.
They parted as good friends, which made me very happy, because in my family
I don’t pray for blessings just for myself, but for grace to come to my family.
When my husband was weak, even during our baptism, when he was weak,
that grace reached my family full of mercy.
There are still many blessings. Because they are with me,
I can say that many have received healing, success in exams, immigration-related blessings, children, and many other graces. But...
They are all in different parts of the world. I have not been able to bring any of them here, that’s why
I am unable to give testimonies, and I am very troubled about that. Someday I believe I will bring them
and then I will be able to give testimonies. Now, what we are doing is a mission work.
Father says the most important work is the mission work, and I firmly believe that
mission work is the best work. I thought about this here. When I go to Canada (my hometown),
every month a cousin or a friend comes here and buys five bundles of the Kreupasanam papers
and sends them to my home. I told my father I will send them. It costs us a good amount,
but we have sacrificed much time to do this. Every month, five bundles of Kreupasanam papers
reach our home in Northville, Canada. Every week there are mostly English newspapers there,
mostly English-speaking, with fewer Malayalis in our area. Every week I am able to give out a bundle
of Kreupasanam papers. Giving them here is not that easy because the weather is harsh.
Our area is not near Toronto; it’s a bit farther, an area where temperatures go down to minus 30.
It’s quite a challenge to distribute the papers. Even though I have given them in churches there,
I did not feel it was very effective because faithful people who come to church
have already visited Lourdes, Fatima, and other places. They are more spiritually alive than I am.
So, instead of giving to them, when I think about mission work personally, I feel like Apostle Paul.
He worked among the Gentiles, and that’s how I feel I should work.
With that personal conviction, I go out to the streets, the transit places in Canada — bus stops and cars,
walking along the streets of Canada, in winter or whatever the weather — handing out the Kreupasanam papers.
It is not easy, as I said before.
It’s a bit difficult. My hands are very sensitive. When the temperature goes to -30,
when the temperature is around -20 or less, my hands get numb. When I give out the papers and keep walking,
my hands turn blue and start to dry inside. Then they crack, and later they get even worse.
After that, I give out a few more papers, and my hands get numb and cracked again.
I continue doing this, even though my hands dry and crack like this.
Now the next thing is, some people will receive it, some won’t. Some will argue with us,
but they all usually talk quite politely.
After that, it depends on what happens. Some people throw it away, some Canadians don’t bother with it.
They say “If you want, take it; if not, no need.” But some others receive it and then throw it away.
When I notice that, I don’t just give the paper and leave — I stay there for a while.
I watch them, and after everyone leaves, that particular person also leaves,
I check all the dustbins. It’s not easy like I say — even homeless people don’t do that.
It’s a bit difficult. Sometimes even the homeless don’t do it. I check all the dustbins,
and every waste bin — all the waste is there. Everyone sees this — I check all the dustbins —
and there’s no paper or even a single container in there. When they take the paper and throw it away,
it’s really shameful. But more than that, beyond what others think,
my God will think about me. That’s what I think. It’s a very anointed thing for me,
so I’m happy about it. Though it’s shameful, as Father said, it’s a status depromotion —
everyone does it shamelessly in front of me, but I feel a tremendous anointing. I continue doing this.
That’s it, that will continue until then. That means not even one paper I give should go to waste —
it is a channel that leads someone to eternity. That’s how I see the Kreupasanam paper. So, I am very strict
that none of it should be wasted. Every paper I give, I have prayed over it with faith and sprinkled salt on it.
On each paper, I write my name and phone number. Many call me, sharing their problems and issues,
and many I am able to bring closer to Jesus through that. That’s how it is.
Then online, I do mission work daily for 400 to 500 people. Using three mobile phones,
I send testimonies, daily bread messages, and faith encouragement. Sometimes I spend three and a half hours a day for this.
I get tremendous joy from this, and through this many people have come to faith. Many people have come,
worldwide, when I introduce myself and give the paper, I say I am a Marian missionary.
That is my favourite way to introduce myself, and I love saying it. So, worldwide, as a Marian mission...
I am able to work.
I am able to bring many people to Jesus through Mary. Many people have taken faith commitments through me.
I don’t just get them to commit, I also follow up. I keep in touch with them occasionally.
That’s how I work.
Now for merciful works.
Mainly, the people there know to give food to the homeless. Like here,
there are people who are homeless there too.
But really, it is said that you shouldn’t give food directly to the homeless.
Many people give food through food banks, but if we do that,
we cannot tell them it’s done in Jesus’ name. Father says,
if we just give it casually, that is charity work, but if we say it is done in Jesus’ name, that becomes a grace work.
So I like doing grace work. That’s why I connect correctly with every homeless person in front of me
and every week bring many people to faith. The food I give them sometimes
we ourselves might not even have eaten. But I buy the food for them and tell them it is in Jesus’ name,
and they say, “Praise the Lord. Hallelujah, God bless you,” when I give it.
I do this every week.
Also, an important thing at our church — the English church is very active, but it is an RC church.
Me, my husband, and our two children are able to be very active there.
There is an organization in church called Street Ministry, which means we go to the streets, prepare food,
and give it to the homeless. I am part of that and able to work.
It’s part of my faith commitment work, and also part of the merciful work.
Because of that, many people have come into contact with me. Many have contacted me.
They call me for many problems. I still don’t know how it’s happening, but many people are struggling a lot.
Many have suffered a lot before coming here, they have debt,
and many are from various parts of India. Many have to pay rent or fees or their phone bills...
We have been able to help by providing groceries and such, but
as I said earlier, whether it is a small thing or a big thing,
we always do it telling them it is done in Jesus’ name. When I think about it now, I wonder how all this was possible.
But when it comes to our own affairs, we sometimes take loans from many people and do these things.
Still, in the end, God doubles back what we have done and blesses us.
When I was at home, as part of the mission’s outreach, I was able to reach some poor families.
They still don’t know about us, no one knows what we are doing. I’m only saying this because I was asked.
There are many families whom we are able to support with a fixed provision even now from our poverty.
But the Lord is the owner and He doubles everything and gives it back to us.
When I say it’s a spiritual growth, nothing interrupts our family prayers or the Holy Mass.
No matter how busy we are, for the sake of prayer, we do everything. Even if it’s two weeks,
although it’s an English parish, we go and confess, sometimes twice in two weeks or once a week.
Likewise, attending Mass is something I never miss. The Holy Mass is something I never skip in my life.
We are in an English parish, not Malayalam, and it’s far from home.
The winter is very harsh here, so if my husband is not available, I either drive or take the bus.
I have even walked in the minus temperatures for half an hour to three hours to attend Mass. No matter what happens, I never skip Holy Mass.
That means I sometimes have to compromise a lot. Even at my workplace, everyone runs to get their shifts covered.
But when they offer me shifts, I say I have to go to Mass, and if I have attended Mass, I tell them I am not available.
Because of that, others may feel they lose out, but I feel I gain. I have been affected in many ways by this.
But still, I am not ready to give up even a bit. I need to receive Jesus every day.
Also, where I am, by my words, actions, and attitude,
I show that I am a Christian, a person of Christian faith, a follower of Jesus, so others say I am a child of Jesus.
People tell me, "You are very spiritual, you are holy, you are very religious."
They say this because of the attitude I carry here. I am clear that I must always use the name of Jesus rightly.
If anyone says anything wrongly, even if they are my superiors, I tell them, "This is the name of my Lord, my Lord is holy, use it reverently. This is wrong; this must not be done."
Then they start following me. I don’t have to look at others; as my father said, I only think about how God thinks about me.
I always keep this in mind and say the same to others.
Likewise, on Sundays at Mass, even those who have committed to the faith but don’t come for Sunday Mass, or don’t go on Good Friday or Easter, I correct them and tell them it is wrong.
I have to stop here due to lack of time.
If you ask me why Kreupasanam?, I say it is not just a place to get PR or come to Canada.
This is all for God, to give to God, to take a stand of sacrifice. It is a place that taught me this.
If you ask why Kreupasanam, I say Grace Home is where my Lord gave me the opportunity to see Jesus in the suffering,
to help those who suffer in the name of Jesus, and to bring them to Jesus.
So always, this is my heaven, my honor, my heaven on earth is Grace Home. Thank you Jesus Christ, thank you so much Mother Mary, love you.
Psalm 138, third verse: Your name and promises are excellent.
On the day I called and pleaded, I received an answer there. Courage filled my soul and strengthened me.
We have heard a great testimony of manifestation.
The testimony is long, but let us understand that the grace is that great. This is a story of great miracles in the life of this immigrant.
Let us thank Jesus and the Holy Mother.
They received PR, birth certificates, and above all,
for two differently-abled brothers, deaf and mute, after seven years they were blessed with a child.
Tiji and her husband prayed for them and made many efforts to bring others closer to the love of God.
Even in -30 degree weather, they kept doing their work out of love for Jesus. This all reflects their love for Jesus.
They did many things and for all their efforts, let us give a big round of applause to Jesus and the Holy Mother and present this testimony.
